item.content:encoded:
A hurricane forecast is predicting dangerous conditions for the Pensacola area, according to reporting from El Nuevo Herald. The forecast calls for sustained winds up to 120 mph in the Pensacola vicinity, along with a storm surge that could reach 7 feet.

Those conditions would be consistent with a major hurricane impact. Residents in Escambia County and surrounding areas should monitor National Hurricane Center updates and heed any evacuation orders from local emergency management.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias approaches central Gulf Coast at major hurricane strength; Pensacola area under warnings
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the central Gulf Coast this morning with sustained winds near 110 mph and intensifying toward major hurricane status. The storm is positioned approximately 245 miles south of Pensacola and moving north-northeast at 15 mph, according to weather reports. Storm Surge Warnings and Hurricane Warnings remain in effect…
item.content:encoded:
Hurricane Isaias is bearing down on the central Gulf Coast this morning with sustained winds near 110 mph and intensifying toward major hurricane status. The storm is positioned approximately 245 miles south of Pensacola and moving north-northeast at 15 mph, according to weather reports.

Storm Surge Warnings and Hurricane Warnings remain in effect for the central Gulf Coast, including areas from Ocean Springs, Mississippi to the Bay/Gulf County line in Florida. The National Weather Service is urging residents in warned areas to complete all preparations immediately, as the window for final safety measures is narrowing to just a few hours.

As Isaias continues its northward track, the Pensacola area faces the threat of dangerous winds, storm surge, and heavy rainfall. Residents and businesses are advised to secure loose outdoor items, ensure emergency supplies are stocked, and finalize evacuation plans if ordered to leave.

item.content:encoded:

The purpose of the press conference has not been disclosed in the advisory. Credentialed media interested in attending were asked to RSVP to Gabriela.Alvarado@eog.myflorida.com.

item.content:encoded: Alabama Governor Kay Ivey has issued a mandatory evacuation order for visitors and non-residents in South Baldwin County and Mobile County as Hurricane Isaias approaches the Gulf Coast. item.content:encoded:
Escambia County is opening emergency shelters today for both the general public and residents with special needs as the area prepares for potential power disruptions, according to a Citizen Portal alert.

The county is urging residents to take advantage of the shelter openings and prepare for possible outages. Officials are also highlighting an opportunity for residents to refill medications during the emergency response period.

Shelters will accommodate both general populations and those requiring specialized care or support during the weather event.

item.content:encoded:
Taylor Dental has partnered with PCS Outreach Ministries to provide school supplies to more than 1,000 families in Escambia County ahead of the new school year. The collaboration, which spans multiple years, distributed supplies to 1,033 Pensacola-area families, according to the organizations.

The back-to-school event represents an ongoing commitment by the dental practice to support local students and families in the community. PCS Outreach Ministries, which focuses on serving Pensacola residents, worked alongside Taylor Dental to organize and execute the initiative.

The partnership highlights how local businesses can address a practical need for families preparing children for school, when the cost of supplies can strain household budgets.

item.content:encoded:

The closure affects all non-essential staff at the installation, which employs thousands of military and civilian workers. The base regularly adjusts operations ahead of tropical systems that threaten the area.

Listeners should monitor local weather updates for the latest track and impact forecasts for Hurricane Isaias as it approaches Northwest Florida.

item.content:encoded: Santa Rosa County is opening its sand distribution sites to help residents prepare for Hurricane Isaias, which is forecast to make landfall Friday. Residents should gather their bags and head to the distribution sites as soon as possible to ensure they have adequate protection before the hurricane arrives.

item.title: Escambia County shellfish harvest area closing ahead of Hurricane Isaias

The precautionary closure is designed to protect both public health and the shellfish resource during the storm. Big Lagoon, located in Escambia County, is…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services is temporarily closing the Big Lagoon Shellfish Harvest Area effective at sunset Thursday as Hurricane Isaias approaches the region.

The precautionary closure is designed to protect both public health and the shellfish resource during the storm. Big Lagoon, located in Escambia County, is a significant shellfish harvesting area for local watermen and commercial operators.

According to WKRG News 5, the closure will remain in effect until conditions stabilize and state officials determine it's safe to resume harvesting. Residents and commercial harvesters in the area should be aware of the temporary restriction.

item.title: Florida Health Department Proposes Relaxing School Immunization Requirements
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health held a public hearing Thursday on proposed changes to school and childcare immunization rules that would remove requirements for four vaccines while keeping others in place. Under the proposal, hepatitis B, varicella (chickenpox), Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines would no…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health held a public hearing Thursday on proposed changes to school and childcare immunization rules that would remove requirements for four vaccines while keeping others in place.

Under the proposal, hepatitis B, varicella (chickenpox), Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines would no longer be mandated for school or childcare entry in Florida. The changes would align Department rules with state statute, according to a press release from the Department. Immunizations for polio, diphtheria, measles, rubella, pertussis, mumps, and tetanus would remain required.

State Surgeon General Dr. Joseph A. Ladapo framed the proposal as expanding parental choice. "Parents know their children best, and they should be the ultimate decision-makers about their children's health," Ladapo said in a statement. The Department emphasized that removing rule requirements does not prevent parents from choosing to vaccinate their children with the affected vaccines, and that religious and medical exemptions from immunization requirements remain available under Florida law.

The public hearing is one step in Florida's rulemaking process and does not constitute final adoption of the rule. The proposal also includes updates to immunization forms, exemption procedures, and compliance reporting requirements.

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College will shut down all campus locations starting at 4 p.m. today and remain closed through Saturday, October 10, due to Hurricane Isaias, the college announced Thursday morning.

The closure affects all classes, events, campus activities, and online courses. Emergency personnel will remain on campus during the closure. The college is taking the precaution as the hurricane approaches the region.

Library services are expected to resume Sunday, October 11, and will be available to students. The college will provide updates on its social media platforms, website at pensacolastate.edu, and through PSC Alert if conditions change.

item.title: DOH-Escambia Opens Special Needs Shelter at Wagner Road Location
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County opened a Special Needs Shelter on Thursday at the Marie K. Young-Wedgewood Community Center and Park, located at 6405 Wagner Road in Pensacola. The shelter is designed to serve people with stable impairments or disabilities whose care needs go beyond basic first aid available at general shelters.…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Escambia County opened a Special Needs Shelter on Thursday at the Marie K. Young-Wedgewood Community Center and Park, located at 6405 Wagner Road in Pensacola. The shelter is designed to serve people with stable impairments or disabilities whose care needs go beyond basic first aid available at general shelters.

The facility opened at 3 p.m. today and can accommodate residents whose medical requirements exceed what standard emergency shelters provide. DOH-Escambia notes that nursing staff at the location is limited, so shelter attendees are strongly encouraged to bring a caregiver. Staff will be available to assist when medical needs exceed a caregiver's training or knowledge.

Residents planning to use the shelter should arrive prepared with bedding, food and water for up to seven days, medications and medical supplies for that same period, toiletries, and clothing. Each person should plan to bring one gallon of water per day for a week-long stay. Service animals are permitted in the shelter space; other pets will be housed in a separate animal shelter area at the same location. More details about pet requirements are available on the Escambia County Emergency Management website.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County officials announced Thursday that evacuation orders will be issued later in the day as Hurricane Isaias continues to intensify, according to Miramar News.

The orders will affect Pensacola Beach, Perdido Key, and other low-lying areas throughout the county. Residents in those zones are urged to monitor official channels for updates and prepare to leave as soon as orders are formally announced.

This is a developing situation. More details on the evacuation timeline and specific zones will be released as the day progresses. Residents should have a plan in place and monitor Escambia County emergency management for official guidance.

item.title: Santa Rosa Opens Special Needs Shelter at Milton Community Center Friday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will open a Special Needs Shelter beginning Friday, October 9, at 8 a.m. at the Clyde L. Gracey Community Center in Milton, located at 5629 Byrom St. The shelter is designed for people whose age, frailty, mobility, functional, or medical disability makes them vulnerable in disaster situations.…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County will open a Special Needs Shelter beginning Friday, October 9, at 8 a.m. at the Clyde L. Gracey Community Center in Milton, located at 5629 Byrom St.

The shelter is designed for people whose age, frailty, mobility, functional, or medical disability makes them vulnerable in disaster situations. Those eligible include individuals with pre-existing medical conditions who have been able to maintain daily living activities at home before a disaster.

Attendees should bring a caregiver with them, as nursing staff at the shelter is limited and available primarily to assist with medical needs beyond a caregiver's training. Residents should pack bedding, medications and medical supplies for seven days, non-perishable food and water (one gallon per person per day for up to a week), toiletries, and clothing. Service animals are permitted in the shelter; other pets will be housed in a separate animal shelter area at the location.

For more information about pet disaster preparedness requirements, residents can visit the Santa Rosa County website. Those with questions can contact the Florida Department of Health in Santa Rosa County at PIO.CHD57@flhealth.gov or 850-851-8929.

item.title: Milton declares local emergency, closes offices Friday ahead of Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton is preparing for Hurricane Isaias by declaring a state of local emergency and shutting down municipal operations Friday, October 9, according to a release from Mayor Heather Lindsay's office Thursday. All city offices will close Friday, and several services are being adjusted. Sanitation collections will run from 7 a.m. to noon,…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton is preparing for Hurricane Isaias by declaring a state of local emergency and shutting down municipal operations Friday, October 9, according to a release from Mayor Heather Lindsay's office Thursday.

All city offices will close Friday, and several services are being adjusted. Sanitation collections will run from 7 a.m. to noon, and residents are asked to place carts curbside early and secure them immediately after pickup. The community center is cancelling all activities beginning at 4:30 p.m. Thursday, and city parks will close Friday and remain closed until further notice. The city is also pausing late fees on utility bills for October 8–9.

Milton's Clyde L. Gracey Community Center at 5629 Byrom Street will open as a pet-friendly emergency shelter at 8 a.m. Friday, with no preregistration required. Residents should bring identification, medications, water, snacks, bedding and personal essentials. Those bringing pets need carriers, proof of vaccinations, and pet supplies; meals will not be provided. Transportation assistance to shelters is available by calling (850) 983-4636 while winds remain below tropical storm force.

City officials are coordinating with Santa Rosa County Emergency Management and urge residents to complete storm preparations, secure outdoor items, avoid flooded roads, and monitor official weather updates. For the latest information, visit miltonfl.org or the City of Milton's Facebook page.

This action comes as part of emergency preparedness measures tied to weather or other conditions affecting the region. Affected personnel should monitor official base communications and Okaloosa County emergency management for updates and further instructions.

item.title: Pensacola International Airport closing Friday ahead of Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola International Airport will suspend commercial flight operations beginning at 10 a.m. Friday as Hurricane Isaias approaches the Gulf Coast, according to an announcement from the airport. The closure is part of a broader preparation effort across Northwest Florida as the storm tracks toward a Gulf Coast landfall. A second airport in the…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola International Airport will suspend commercial flight operations beginning at 10 a.m. Friday as Hurricane Isaias approaches the Gulf Coast, according to an announcement from the airport.

The closure is part of a broader preparation effort across Northwest Florida as the storm tracks toward a Gulf Coast landfall. A second airport in the region has also announced similar precautions, though specific details on that facility were not immediately available.

The 10 a.m. Friday closure gives the airport time to secure facilities and allow passengers and staff to seek shelter before conditions deteriorate. Travelers with flights scheduled during or after the closure window should contact their airlines for rebooking options.
